entries.name: CACNA1C rs1006737
entries.summary: Genome-wide significant risk allele for bipolar disorder and schizophrenia, each A copy raising odds only ~1.1–1.2x. Lifetime risk stays low for almost every carrier; useful for research, not prediction.

entries.name: CYP2C9*3
entries.summary: Strongly reduced-function allele; larger effect than *2 on warfarin dose requirement.

entries.name: CFH Y402H
entries.summary: C allele is the main common risk factor for age-related macular degeneration (~2.5x heterozygous, ~6x homozygous). Smoking multiplies the risk.

entries.name: 9p21 CAD locus
entries.summary: Most replicated common coronary artery disease variant. GG ~1.5–1.9x CAD risk vs AA; effect independent of lipids.

entries.name: MSMB rs10993994
entries.summary: T allele raises prostate cancer risk ~1.25x per allele and lowers PSA-independent MSMB expression.

entries.name: CYP2C19*17
entries.summary: Increased-function promoter variant. Rapid/ultrarapid metabolism of CYP2C19 substrates; lower SSRI exposure, PPIs may need higher dose.

entries.name: ADH1B*2 (Arg48His)
entries.summary: T allele = fast alcohol-to-acetaldehyde conversion, flushing, strong protection against alcohol dependence.

CT.label: fast ADH1B, flushing likely, lower dependence risk

entries.name: SLC30A8 R325W
entries.summary: The common C (Arg325) allele of the beta-cell zinc transporter ZnT8 raises type 2 diabetes risk ~1.15x per copy; the T (Trp) allele is mildly protective.

entries.name: 9p21 rs1333049
entries.summary: Second tag SNP of the 9p21 CAD locus, in strong LD with rs10757278.

entries.name: FKBP5 rs1360780
entries.summary: T allele slows the shut-off of the cortisol stress response. In people with childhood adversity it is linked to higher PTSD and depression risk (a gene-environment interaction); alone it predicts little.

CT.label: slower cortisol recovery; matters mainly after trauma

TT.label: slower cortisol recovery; matters mainly after trauma

entries.name: KIBRA rs17070145
entries.summary: T allele carriers performed better on episodic memory tests in the original and several replication studies; the effect is small and not found in every cohort.

entries.name: MC4R rs17782313
entries.summary: C allele near MC4R, an appetite-regulating gene, raises BMI by ~0.2 kg/m² per copy and is linked to larger meals and snacking; modest type 2 diabetes effect.

CC.label: higher BMI and appetite (~1.2x obesity risk)

entries.name: CYP2C9*2
entries.summary: Reduced-function allele. Slower clearance of warfarin, phenytoin, some NSAIDs.

entries.name: HFE H63D
entries.summary: Milder haemochromatosis variant; matters mainly as compound heterozygote with C282Y.

GG.label: H63D homozygous: mild iron loading possible

entries.name: COL1A1 Sp1 (rs1800012)
entries.summary: A allele (the 's' allele, T on the gene's strand) alters type I collagen production; meta-analyses link it to lower bone density and more osteoporotic fractures, and to some ligament injuries. Weight-bearing exercise, calcium and vitamin D matter more.

AA.label: ss, lower bone density, ~1.8x vertebral fracture odds

entries.name: TPMT*2
entries.summary: Loss-of-function allele; thiopurine (azathioprine, mercaptopurine) myelosuppression risk.

entries.name: HFE C282Y
entries.summary: Main hereditary haemochromatosis variant. AA (C282Y homozygous) = high iron-overload risk; check ferritin/transferrin saturation. Carriers are usually unaffected.

entries.name: MTHFR C677T
entries.summary: TT (here AA on forward strand) reduces enzyme activity ~70%, raises homocysteine when folate is low. Clinical impact is small with adequate folate; not a reason for high-dose supplements.

entries.name: NAT2*5 (rs1801280)
entries.summary: Slow-acetylator allele. Affects isoniazid, hydralazine, sulfasalazine toxicity.

CC.label: two slow alleles: slow acetylator likely

entries.name: PPARG Pro12Ala
entries.summary: The common C (Pro) allele carries slightly higher T2D risk; G (Ala) is mildly protective and linked to better insulin sensitivity.

entries.name: MC1R R151C
entries.summary: Red-hair/fair-skin allele; raises melanoma risk ~2x per allele independent of pigmentation.

TT.label: homozygous: red hair likely, ~4x melanoma risk

entries.name: ACTN3 R577X
entries.summary: T (577X) is a stop codon: XX people make no alpha-actinin-3 in fast-twitch muscle fibres. RR is over-represented among sprint and power athletes, XX slightly among endurance athletes. Training matters far more.

entries.name: HLA-DQ2.5 tag
entries.summary: Tags HLA-DQ2.5, present in ~90% of coeliac disease patients. Absence nearly rules coeliac disease out; presence alone is common (~25% of Europeans).

TT.label: two DQ2.5 haplotypes: higher coeliac risk

entries.name: CYP2D6*4
entries.summary: Most common null allele of CYP2D6 in Europeans. Affects codeine, tramadol, tamoxifen, many antidepressants and antipsychotics. Star-allele calling from arrays is incomplete.

entries.name: DPYD*2A
entries.summary: Splice variant abolishing DPD activity. Carriers are at serious risk of fluoropyrimidine (5-FU, capecitabine) toxicity; CPIC recommends dose reduction or avoidance.

entries.name: SLCO1B1*5 (c.521T>C)
entries.summary: Reduced hepatic uptake of statins; higher simvastatin exposure and myopathy risk.

entries.name: CYP2C19*2
entries.summary: Loss-of-function allele. Carriers metabolise clopidogrel, some PPIs and several SSRIs more slowly.

entries.name: APOE rs429358 (ε4 determinant)
entries.summary: C allele defines APOE ε4 (with rs7412 T = ε2). ε4 raises late-onset Alzheimer's and cardiovascular risk; one copy ~3x, two copies ~10x AD odds. Not on AncestryDNA/MyHeritage chips.

entries.name: COMT Val158Met
entries.summary: Met (A) allele = slower dopamine clearance in prefrontal cortex ('worrier': better memory, more stress sensitivity); Val (G) = 'warrior'. Effects are small and context dependent.

entries.name: Lactase persistence -13910C>T
entries.summary: A allele (T on the minus strand) keeps lactase active in adults. GG on forward strand = lactase non-persistence, lactose intolerance likely in adulthood.

entries.name: KCNJ11 E23K
entries.summary: T (Lys23) allele of the beta-cell potassium channel lowers insulin secretion: ~1.15x type 2 diabetes risk per copy. The same channel is the target of sulfonylurea drugs.

entries.name: BDNF Val66Met
entries.summary: T (Met66) allele lowers activity-dependent release of BDNF, a growth factor for neurons. Linked to slightly weaker episodic memory and a smaller hippocampus in some studies; links to depression and anxiety are inconsistent. Exercise raises BDNF whatever the genotype.

CT.label: Val/Met, possibly slightly weaker episodic memory

entries.name: APOA5 -1131T>C
entries.summary: G (minor) allele raises triglycerides and modestly raises CAD risk; interacts with dietary fat.

entries.name: ALDH2*2
entries.summary: A allele inactivates ALDH2: alcohol flush, higher oesophageal cancer risk with drinking. Rare outside East Asia.

entries.name: APOE rs7412 (ε2 determinant)
entries.summary: T allele defines APOE ε2 (protective for AD, but ε2/ε2 predisposes to type III hyperlipoproteinaemia). Read together with rs429358.

entries.name: CYP1A2*1F
entries.summary: AA genotype = fast caffeine metabolism; C carriers slower. Weak evidence for cardiovascular interaction with high coffee intake.

entries.name: TCF7L2 rs7903146
entries.summary: Strongest common type 2 diabetes risk variant. Each T allele raises T2D odds ~1.4x; TT ~2x. Modifiable through weight, diet and activity.

entries.name: FOXE1 rs965513
entries.summary: A allele raises thyroid cancer risk (~1.7x per allele) and is linked to hypothyroidism/TSH levels.

entries.name: VKORC1 -1639G>A
entries.summary: Promoter variant lowering VKORC1 expression; strongest common predictor of warfarin sensitivity.

entries.name: FTO rs9939609
entries.summary: Largest common obesity variant: each A allele adds about 0.4 kg/m² BMI (~1.3x obesity odds) and raises type 2 diabetes risk through weight. Regular physical activity blunts the effect by about a third.

AA.label: ~1.7x obesity risk, ~3 kg heavier on average

conditions.summary: Facial flushing after alcohol from slow acetaldehyde clearance (ALDH2*2).
The commonest dementia; APOE e4 is the strongest common genetic risk factor.
Joint inflammation or wear; track pain, stiffness and which joints.
Narrowing of the heart arteries by atherosclerosis; the 9p21 locus is the strongest common genetic signal, independent of cholesterol.
Immune reaction to gluten; almost all patients carry HLA-DQ2 or DQ8, so a negative tag nearly rules it out.
Iron overload, mostly in HFE C282Y homozygotes; early diagnosis and venesection prevent organ damage.
Raised homocysteine, often from low folate or B12; MTHFR TT lowers the folate reserve.
Raised blood lipids, the main modifiable driver of coronary artery disease.
Persistently raised blood pressure; the commonest modifiable cardiovascular risk.
Raised blood triglycerides; APOA5 variants raise them further.
Low thyroid hormone; common, easily tested with TSH.
Adult loss of lactase; the MCM6/LCT genotype predicts it well in Europeans.
Death of heart muscle from a blocked coronary artery.
Recurrent headache attacks, often with nausea and light sensitivity.
Chronic high blood sugar from insulin resistance. Common, strongly influenced by weight and activity; TCF7L2 is the largest common genetic effect.
Remnant-lipoprotein disorder seen mostly in APOE e2/e2 carriers with a second trigger.
